title: fix(update): preserve auth policy in candidate rehearsals
body:
Fixes #146017

<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

This PR uses an upstream branch so repository maintainers can push fixes directly.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users updating an installation with Policy `requireExplicitRateLimit` would have candidate validation refused even though `gateway.auth.rateLimit` was configured. The rehearsal replaced the entire auth object, so its own synthetic configuration triggered `policy/gateway-rate-limit-missing`.

Reported by @jj5638521 (#146017).

## Why This Change Was Made

The isolated-config builder now starts with the existing auth object and overrides the isolated authentication fields: token mode, a fresh temporary token, no password, and no Tailscale identity authentication. The strict auth schema has only two secret fields, token and password; both are replaced or removed. This preserves rate limits, identity scopes, and trusted-proxy metadata without maintaining a second list of non-secret fields. Explicitly disabling `allowTailscale` matters because it overrides the default derived from `tailscale.mode`, even when that mode is off.

Gateway binding remains loopback, with the rehearsal's allocated port, TLS disabled, and Tailscale/Control UI disabled. Production configuration is unchanged. Production code grows by six lines to preserve the auth object and keep the credential and alternate-auth overrides explicit.

## User Impact

Candidate rehearsal keeps policy-observed Gateway auth settings such as `rateLimit`, so policy lint no longer refuses updates because the rehearsal discarded them.

**First-hop limitation:** the already-installed 2026.9.3/2026.9.4 driver runs its own rehearsal builder, so that hop may still trip the Policy lint until the corrective release is installed once. This change protects subsequent updates initiated by a driver containing the fix. Published-driver × candidate recovery remains separate work and is not claimed by this PR.

## Evidence

The new regression calls the real rehearsal preparation entry point, reads its serialized config, and runs the registered Policy checks through Doctor's lint runner. Both token and password cases preserve the complete configured rate limit, use a different temporary token, remove the production password SecretRef and ambient Gateway credentials, disable Tailscale identity authentication, retain loopback/port isolation, and leave source config unchanged.

Before the production fix:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/update-candidate-rehearsal.test.ts
Tests  2 failed (2)
checkId: policy/gateway-rate-limit-missing
severity: error
requirement: oc://policy.jsonc/gateway/auth/requireExplicitRateLimit
```

After the fix, both regression cases pass. Focused proof: **393 tests passed across six files** (four routed Vitest shards), followed by a passing final regression rerun. **`node scripts/check-changed.mjs` passed**, including core/test typechecks, lint, formatting, plugin boundaries, and repository guards.

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/update-candidate-rehearsal.test.ts src/infra/update-candidate-canary.test.ts src/infra/update-candidate-rehearsal.resources.test.ts src/commands/doctor-lint.test.ts src/flows/doctor-lint-flow.test.ts extensions/policy/src/doctor/register.test.ts
node scripts/check-changed.mjs
```

### Sibling audit and limitations

Policy Gateway rules read auth mode/rate-limit presence; bind/custom host; Gateway mode/remote URL; Tailscale mode/preserved Funnel; Control UI enablement/host-origin fallback; HTTP endpoint enablement and file/image URL allowlists; and node-command allow/deny lists. HTTP and node fields already survive the outer Gateway spread. Policy does not inspect TLS, port, trusted proxies, identity scopes, or trusted-proxy settings.

Default Doctor lint additionally checks auth availability/ambiguity, authenticated network exposure, node-onboarding URLs, plaintext credentials, and MCP compatibility/public origin. Existing synthetic loopback onboarding and inline-token findings are warnings; candidate lint uses `--severity-min error`. No additional Gateway Policy error-producing synthesis was found, and lint rules were not changed.

The regression uses the existing public-plugin fixture loader to keep Policy implementation files outside the core typecheck graph. It was rerun against the unchanged pre-fix builder and failed with the same finding, then rerun with the fix.

No live Gateway or full published-version update was run. Proof uses synthetic state and the actual Policy lint implementation. The campaign lead reviewed the exact head with Codex: scoped-clean at P1. The native CI watcher reverified head `91b9553a9ced3997d8b30d79e182871d3d5eee2b` as GREEN against [CI run 34700879797](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34700879797).

## ClawSweeper review

The exact-head review found no actionable code or security defects. No code fixups were needed. The campaign lead explicitly accepted landing the future-driver repair: the P1 published-driver/canary proof request and P2 broader upgrade coverage request are deferred with the first-hop limitation above, and the maintainer scope decision is resolved. This PR retains `Fixes #146017` and reporter credit as directed; it does not claim a verified repair of the first hop from an already-installed 2026.9.3/2026.9.4 driver. No re-review was requested because code is unchanged.
